title_as_printed: Isopiestic molalities m (column header m/(mol kg-1); columns NaCl, MgSO4, NiSO4 printed three times side by side; blocks 383.14 K and 413.22 K)
property_note: reference salt NaCl; value = MgSO4 molality in isopiestic equilibrium, value2 = NaCl reference molality of the same equilibrium. NiSO4 (out of scope, not in the six-ion set) was equilibrated in the same vessel and is printed in the same row: kept in the CSV, not mapped.
pressure_note: not stated (isopiestic equilibrium with a common vapour phase in a sealed pressure vessel; pressure not tabulated)

value2.what: NaCl reference-electrolyte molality in the same isopiestic equilibrium (measured)

composition.other_species: NaCl reference solution in the partner isopiestic cup (column 'NaCl m mol/kg'); NiSO4 test solution in a third cup (column 'NiSO4 m mol/kg', out of scope)

skip_rows.reason: temperature label rows (also carried by group_rows)
MgSO4 cell printed as a dash (MgSO4 precipitated, no MgSO4 datum); the row holds only the NaCl-NiSO4 pair, which is out of scope

extra_unmapped: NiSO4 m mol/kg (NiSO4 isopiestic molality; NiSO4 outside the six-ion set)
notes: Three side-by-side column groups (NaCl, MgSO4, NiSO4) per temperature block; stacked per block left group first (top to bottom), then middle, then right. A printed em dash means the salt was not in solution (precipitated); written as '-'. Rows 44 and 48 (413.22 K, NiSO4 '-') are MgSO4-NaCl pairs with no NiSO4 value. Authors: for molalities above 1.0 mol/kg the last digit is not significant; molalities accurate to 0.25 per cent or better. The 383.14 K results come from three separate loadings of the apparatus. The authors compute phi from eq. (1) phi_x = m_r phi_r / m_x (both salts taken to give two ions) with phi_r of NaCl from Silvester and Pitzer (1977); phi is not printed in the table.
